proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\), let \(\mu\) be Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb R^d\), and represent a randomized rule by a vector \(p=(p_A)_{A\in\mathcal A}\) satisfying
\[
 p_A\geq 0,\qquad \sum_{A\in\mathcal A}p_A=1
 \quad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\tag{1}
\]
Call the set of these vectors \(\mathscr K\).  This representation is exact because \(\mathcal A\) is finite.  We first establish compactness rather than impose it.

For \(j\geq1\), let \(B_j=[-j,j]^d\), and choose a countable orthonormal basis \((e_{jk})_{k\geq1}\) of \(L^2(B_j)\).  Since \(0\leq p_A\leq1\),
\[
 \|p_A\|_{L^2(B_j)}\leq \mu(B_j)^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
Given a sequence in \(\mathscr K\), diagonal extraction over the countable triples \((A,j,k)\) makes every coefficient \(\langle p_A,e_{jk}\rangle_{L^2(B_j)}\) converge.  Bessel's inequality and (2) identify the limiting coefficients with an element \(p_A^{(j)}\in L^2(B_j)\), and the extracted sequence converges weakly to it.  The limits on nested boxes agree, because a test function on \(B_j\), extended by zero, is a test function on \(B_{j+1}\).  They therefore define a measurable function \(p_A\) on \(\mathbb R^d\).  For every nonnegative \(q\in L^2(B_j)\), weak convergence gives \(\int_{B_j}p_Aq\,d\mu\geq0\).  Taking \(q=(p_A)_-\), applying the same argument to \(1-p_A\), and testing \(\sum_Ap_A-1\) and its negative prove (1) for the limit.  The bounded differences of the countably many displayed coefficients define a metric for the coordinatewise local weak topology on the sets bounded by (2).  The diagonal argument proves sequential compactness in this metric, hence compactness of \(\mathscr K\).

For \(v\in V\), \(h\in D_v\), and \(g\in H_r\), define
\[
 c_{v,h}(p)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\sum_{A\ni v}p_A(w)\,dw,
 \qquad
 r_g(p)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\sum_A\ell(A)p_A(w)\,dw.
\tag{3}
\]
The positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\) makes each translated Gaussian density square integrable on every \(B_j\).  Local weak convergence therefore gives convergence of both integrals over \(B_j\).  The contribution outside \(B_j\) is bounded by the corresponding Gaussian tail for \(c_{v,h}\), and by \(D\) times that tail for \(r_g\).  Letting \(j\to\infty\) proves that every functional in (3) is continuous on \(\mathscr K\).

Consequently,
\[
 \mathscr K_\eta=
 \bigcap_{v\in V}\bigcap_{h\in D_v}
 \{p\in\mathscr K:c_{v,h}(p)\geq1-\eta\}
\tag{4}
\]
is compact.  It is nonempty because the rule reporting \(V\) surely belongs to it.  The map \(p\mapsto\sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p)\) is a supremum of continuous functions and is therefore lower semicontinuous.  It attains its minimum on (4).  All Gaussian shifts with covariance \(\Sigma\succ0\) are equivalent to Lebesgue measure, so changing the finitely many coordinates on one common null set turns the minimizing representative into a Markov kernel valid for every mean.  This proves primal attainment.

We next derive the dual and its exact finite-atomic exhaustion.  Let
\[
 \alpha_v=\sum_{j=1}^{J_v}a_{vj}\delta_{h_{vj}},
 \quad a_{vj}\geq0,\quad h_{vj}\in D_v,
 \qquad
 \beta=\sum_{i=1}^{I}b_i\delta_{g_i},
 \quad b_i\geq0,\quad \sum_i b_i=1,\quad g_i\in H_r,
\tag{5}
\]
and set
\[
 a_v(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,\alpha_v(dh),
 \qquad
 b(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\,\beta(dg).
\tag{6}
\]
The Lagrangian for the risk epigraph and the coverage inequalities is
\[
 (1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int\sum_{A\subseteq V}p_A(w)
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}dw.
\tag{7}
\]
At each \(w\), (1) ranges over a finite simplex.  Choosing the first minimizing action in a fixed enumeration is measurable, so minimization of (7) gives
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 =(1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int\min_{A\subseteq V}
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}dw.
\tag{8}
\]
For every \(p\in\mathscr K_\eta\), Tonelli's theorem applies to the nonnegative Gaussian mixtures in (6), and (3), (5), and (7) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 &\leq \sum_i b_i r_{g_i}(p)
   +\sum_{v,j}a_{vj}\{(1-\eta)-c_{v,h_{vj}}(p)\}\\
 &\leq \sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Thus every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate.

To prove exhaustion, fix \(t<M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  The open sets
\[
 \{p:r_g(p)>t\},\quad g\in H_r,
 \qquad
 \{p:c_{v,h}(p)<1-\eta\},\quad v\in V,\ h\in D_v,
\tag{10}
\]
cover \(\mathscr K\): an honest rule has supremum risk at least \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)>t\), while a nonhonest rule violates one inequality in (4).  Compactness gives a finite subcover with risk points \(g_1,\ldots,g_I\) and coverage points \((v_j,h_j)\), \(j=1,\ldots,J\).  The compact convex set
\[
 Y=\left\{
 \bigl((r_{g_i}(p)-t)_{i\leq I},
 ((1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p))_{j\leq J}\bigr):p\in\mathscr K
 \right\}
\tag{11}
\]
is disjoint from the closed negative orthant.  Let \((y_*,z_*)\) minimize \(\|y-z\|_2^2\) over \(y\in Y\) and \(z\) in that orthant, and put \(n=y_*-z_*\).  Coordinatewise projection gives \(n\geq0\), \(n'z_*=0\), and \(n'y_*=\|n\|_2^2>0\).  The first-order inequality for minimization over the convex set \(Y\) gives \(n'y\geq n'y_*\) for every \(y\in Y\).  Hence there are \(\gamma_i,\zeta_j\geq0\), not all zero, and \(q>0\) such that
\[
 \sum_i\gamma_i\{r_{g_i}(p)-t\}
 +\sum_j\zeta_j\{(1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p)\}
 \geq q
 \quad\text{for every }p\in\mathscr K.
\tag{12}
\]
For the rule reporting \(V\), every coverage deficit in (12) equals \(-\eta\).  Therefore \(G=\sum_i\gamma_i>0\).  Set \(b_i=\gamma_i/G\), and assign mass \(a_j=\zeta_j/G\) to the coverage atom \((v_j,h_j)\).  Dividing (12) by \(G\), taking the infimum over \(p\in\mathscr K\), and using (8) yield
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)\geq t+q/G>t.
\tag{13}
\]
Combining (9) and (13), and then taking \(t\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), proves
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 =\sup_{\alpha,\beta\ {
m finite\ atomic}}\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta).
\tag{14}
\]

It remains to justify the asserted effective restriction on atoms.  Each \(D_v\) is a finite union of rational polyhedra.  Membership in \(H_r\) is a finite Boolean combination of membership in those polyhedra and inequalities
\[
 \inf_{x:Ax\leq b}(h-x)'\Sigma^{-1}(h-x)\geq r^2.
\tag{15}
\]
For every active set of the quadratic program in (15), its primal feasibility, stationarity, complementary slackness, and the displayed value inequality are polynomial equalities and inequalities with rational coefficients.  Taking the finite disjunction over active sets and eliminating the primal and multiplier variables by recursive polynomial sign decomposition gives a rational semialgebraic description of \(H_r\).  The same sign-decomposition recursion decides whether a rational box meets any one of these sets and, when it does, isolates a real-algebraic sample point.  Enumerating rational boxes therefore gives a dense, effectively enumerable family of rationally encoded real-algebraic points in every \(D_v\) and in \(H_r\), including their lower-dimensional components.

If \(x_n\to x\), then translated Gaussian densities converge pointwise, and
\[
 \int|\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n)-\phi_\Sigma(w-x)|\,dw
 =2-2\int\min\{\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n),\phi_\Sigma(w-x)\}\,dw
 \longrightarrow0
\tag{16}
\]
by dominated convergence.  Perturbing finitely many support points within their respective sets, and perturbing the weights to nonnegative rationals while preserving \(\sum_i b_i=1\), consequently makes all mixtures in (6) converge in \(L^1\).  Since
\[
 \left|\min_Ax_A-\min_Ay_A\right|\leq\max_A|x_A-y_A|,
\tag{17}
\]
the dual values in (8) converge as well.  Thus rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points are dense among finite atomic certificates.

Finally, each such dual value is a computable real.  On a rational box, the finitely many Gaussian mixtures have computable uniform derivative bounds, so interval Riemann sums give convergent rational lower and upper bounds for the finite minimum in (8).  Outside the box, the absolute integrand is bounded by \(Db(w)+\sum_va_v(w)\), and the finitely many Gaussian tails have effective outward rational bounds.  Enumerate all atomic certificates and dovetail these two-sided enclosures.  Maintain one certificate and replace it only by a candidate whose certified lower enclosure exceeds the current certificate's certified upper enclosure, choosing at each stage the candidate with the largest certified lower endpoint.  Exact certificate values then increase.  If their limit were below the supremum in (14), a previously enumerated certificate separated from that limit would eventually have its strict advantage certified, a contradiction.  The resulting increasing sequence converges upward to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), and no bounded-support premise has been used.

Assume the effective-compatible-density conclusion.  We describe a single dovetailed algorithm and its stopping recurrence.

At stage \(s\), compute every class \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\) with \(m\leq s\), enumerate all its rational rules and all rational incidence, protected-neighborhood, partition, and rounding receipts of encoding length at most \(s\), and run outward interval integration to precision \(2^{-s}\).  A primal record is accepted only when its finite rational receipts verify a lower coverage enclosure \(c^-_{q,s}\), an upper separated-risk enclosure \(r^+_{q,s}\), and every term in the weighted ledger.  All probability enclosures are intersected with \([0,1]\).  Define
\[
 \rho_{q,s}=\max\{0,1-\eta-c^-_{q,s}\}<1,
 \qquad
 U_{q,s}=r^+_{q,s}+\frac{D\rho_{q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{q,s}}.
\tag{1}
\]
The strict inequality uses \(\eta>0\) and \(c^-_{q,s}\geq0\).  By the exact-repair lemma, the recorded repaired rule is globally honest and
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\leq U_{q,s}.
\tag{2}
\]

In parallel, enumerate all finite atomic duals having rational nonnegative weights, total risk weight one, and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points in the required \(D_v\)'s and in \(H_r\).  Exact polynomial sign tests verify support membership.  The construction in the atomic-duality proof gives, at stage \(s\), a rational outward interval for each enumerated dual value.  Its lower endpoint is a sound lower certificate.  Let
\[
 L_s=\max\{\text{verified dual lower endpoints through stage }s\},
 \qquad
 U_s=\min\{U_{q,t}:q\text{ accepted by some }t\leq s\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Empty maxima and minima are ignored until both collections are nonempty.  Equations (2) and the weak-duality inequality give
\[
 L_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\leq U_s.
\tag{4}
\]

Every check at a fixed stage terminates.  Exact rational polyhedral feasibility and incidence are finite linear-programming computations.  On bounded boxes, interval arithmetic encloses the finitely many Gaussian integrals.  Gaussian tail inequalities enclose the complements.  On an unbounded recession chart, the specified path comparison reduces the outer part to finitely many chart integrals plus the rational ledger; refinement enlarges the protected neighborhoods and decreases the tail and rounding tolerances.  Thus every accepted inequality is a finite comparison of rationals.  This proves replayability and decidability of a stage; it does not infer validity from floating-point output.

We next prove that the stopping test is eventually met.  Let \(K^*\) be the minimizer supplied by atomic duality.  Effective compatible density gives \(q_m\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\) with
\[
 c(q_m)\geq1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m),\qquad
 r(q_m)\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m),\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}(q_m)\leq\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m).
\tag{5}
\]
For any positive rational \(\zeta\), sufficiently fine outward refinement accepts the same finite record with
\[
 c^-_{q_m,s}\geq c(q_m)-\zeta,
 \qquad
 r^+_{q_m,s}\leq r(q_m)+\zeta.
\tag{6}
\]
This follows from the finite ledger decomposition: compact interval widths, Gaussian tails, chart discrepancies, covariance enclosures, and rational rounding errors are all explicitly refined, while (5) supplies the common recession certificate.  From (1), (5), and (6),
\[
 U_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)+\zeta
 +\frac{D\{\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)+\zeta\}}
 {\eta+\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)+\zeta}.
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\downarrow0\), the right side decreases to the minimax value along the dovetail.  Atomic duality supplies verified lower endpoints increasing to the same value.  Hence some finite stage satisfies \(U_s-L_s\leq\varepsilon\).

For completeness, expose the requested total recursive cost bounds.  Let \(a_i(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the number of new operations of type
\[
 i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\}
\]
performed by the finite stage described above, and let \(b(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the largest bit length of an integer in that stage.  These are computable from the finite enumerations.  Set
\[
 C_i(0)=a_i(\mathfrak G,0),\qquad
 C_i(s+1)=C_i(s)+a_i(\mathfrak G,s+1),
 \qquad
 B(s+1)=\max\{B(s),b(\mathfrak G,s+1)\},
\tag{8}
\]
with \(B(0)=b(\mathfrak G,0)\), and define the decidable stopping index
\[
 s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)
 =\min\{s:L_s,U_s\text{ are defined and }U_s-L_s\leq\varepsilon\}.
\tag{9}
\]
The preceding paragraph proves that the unbounded search in (9) halts for every declared input, so (9) is a total recursive function on the encoded input class.  The advertised receipt is
\[
 N_i(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=C_i\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=B\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\}.
\tag{10}
\]
At the stopping stage, choose the atomic dual attaining \(L_s\) and the repaired primal attaining \(U_s\).  Equations (4) and (9) give the claimed outward gap, while (8)--(10) record finite bounds for every enumerated gluing object, cut, Gaussian enclosure, linear program, and integer bit length.

Let \(L=\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  The relative-interior tangent-lift lemma gives, for every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\), a number \(t_u>0\) such that
\[
 p_0+tBu\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 \quad(0<t\leq t_u).
\tag{1}
\]
By the compatible-observed-law-polytope lemma and fiber-polytope equivalence, each law in (1) has a nonempty finite response-type fiber and hence feasible endpoint programs.  Choose any sequence \(t_k\downarrow0\).  There are only finitely many symbolic branch and primal--dual optimal completions, so a subsequence has one constant completion \(b\).  If \(\psi(p_0)\ne0\), its sign along this subsequence is the frozen base sign.  If \(\psi(p_0)=0\), affinity gives
\[
 \psi(p_0+t_kBu)=t_k\alpha_\psi'Bu.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus the constant completion chooses the weak tangent sign prescribed by \(\alpha_\psi'Bu\); when this number is zero, it is incident to both weak sides.  Passing the finite weak linear inequalities and the finite primal--dual equalities to the limit shows that \(b\in\mathcal B_0\) is a feasible optimal completion at \(u\).  Consequently \(u\in P_{v,b}^0\) for its semantic projection \(v\).  Equivalently, by the already established compatible-lift-completed-cover lemma,
\[
 \bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d.
\tag{3}
\]
Equation (2) also proves directly that equality belongs to every incident completion.

Now consider moving offsets.  For the matrix \(A_\Psi\) whose rows are the active \(\alpha_j'\), the active-cut identity \(\psi_j(p_0)=0\) gives
\[
 c_n=\sqrt n\,A_\Psi\{p_n(0)-p_0\}.
\tag{4}
\]
The local-family affine-hull assumption puts the vector in braces in \(L\), so (4) proves \(c_n\in\mathcal K_0=A_\Psi L\); this membership is derived, not imposed separately.

Suppose \(c_n\to c\in\mathcal K_0\), and let a compact \(C\) avoid every active hyperplane \(c_j+a_j'u=0\).  Finiteness gives
\[
 \delta_C=\min_{u\in C}\min_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
 |c_j+a_j'u|>0,
\tag{5}
\]
with the assertion vacuous when the active set is empty.  Compact-uniform convergence of the moving remainders and \(c_n\to c\) imply, eventually,
\[
 \max_j|c_{n,j}-c_j|+
 \max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|<\delta_C.
\tag{6}
\]
After replacing the right side by \(\delta_C/2\), if necessary, (6) and
\[
 \zeta_{n,j}(u)=c_{n,j}+a_j'u+e_{n,j}(u)
\tag{7}
\]
show that \(\zeta_{n,j}(u)\) and \(c_j+a_j'u\) have the same strict sign for every \(u\in C\) and every active \(j\).  For a cut with nonzero base slack, base convergence and the compact local expansion imply \(p_n(u)\to p_0\) uniformly on \(C\), so its frozen sign is also eventually correct.  A zero-base cut with zero tangent normal is, by the completed-label construction, a fixed tie whose incident symbolic branches have the same retained semantic region.  Hence all semantic branch signs agree, and
\[
 \mathcal V_n(u)=\{v:u\in D_v^0(c)\}
 \quad\text{for every }u\in C
\tag{8}
\]
eventually.

If there are no active cuts, every nonempty completed tangent cell is all of \(\mathbb R^d\).  The definition of the assertion map identifies raw patterns with identical completed tangent regions and retains one representative, so there is one semantic label.  Reporting that singleton surely is honest and has diameter zero.  Nonnegativity of loss then gives \(M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)=0\).

If the active list is nonempty, its members are nonzero rational normals.  A finite union of their hyperplanes cannot contain an open ball, so its complement has a nonempty full-dimensional chamber.  Rational points are dense in that open chamber.  By the global-cover proposition and the convention that fixed ties with identical completed regions have one semantic representative, this strict sign chamber lies in a unique semantic component \(P_{v,b}^0\).  At a rational strict point all of its nonredundant defining inequalities have positive slack.  Scaling within the homogeneous chamber and using \(0\leq\gamma\leq1\) shows that the positive-margin linear program used to define \(i_*\) has optimum \(1\) for at least one component.  Therefore the canonical finite search finds a component with positive margin and returns a rational basic solution \(u_*\) in its strict chamber.  If the active list is empty, the prescribed choice \(u_*=0\) lies in the unique component \(\mathbb R^d\).  Thus in both cases
\[
 \{v:u_*\in D_v^0\}=\{v_*\}.
\tag{1}
\]

Consider a retained rival component
\[
 P_{v,b}^0=\{g:A_{v,b}^0g\leq b_{v,b}^0\},\qquad v\ne v_*.
\tag{2}
\]
It cannot contain \(u_*\), by (1).  Since (2) is exactly the intersection of its displayed closed halfspaces, at least one displayed row \(i\) has the rational gap
\[
 \gamma_{v,b,i}=(A_{v,b}^0u_*-b_{v,b}^0)_i>0.
\tag{3}
\]
That row is nonzero.  The base law has strictly positive cells and \(B\) has full column rank, so
\[
 x'I_0x=\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0
 \quad(x\ne0),
\tag{4}
\]
and hence \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\).  Therefore the row norm \(\|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}\) is positive.  For every \(g\in P_{v,b}^0\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \gamma_{v,b,i}
 &\leq (A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}(u_*-g)\\
 &\leq \|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}
       \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
If the rational bisection receipt gives \(s_{v,b,i}\geq\|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}>0\), (5) yields
\[
 \inf_{g\in P_{v,b}^0}\|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \geq\frac{\gamma_{v,b,i}}{s_{v,b,i}}=\rho_{v,b}>0.
\tag{6}
\]
There are finitely many rival components, so the minimum defining \(\rho_0\) is positive; if there is no rival, it equals the included value \(1\).  Since \(r_0=\min\{r_{\mathrm{req}},\rho_0\}\), taking the minimum of (6) over the components of every rival semantic union gives
\[
 \inf_{v\ne v_*}\inf_{g\in D_v^0}
 \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}\geq\rho_0\geq r_0.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (1) and (7) put \(u_*\) in \(H_{r_0}\).  All chamber, row-gap, norm-enclosure, and minimum operations are finite rational computations, which proves the asserted exact certificates and the nonempty separated domain without a causal margin premise.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), write \(p=p(P)\), and let \(\mathsf C=\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\}\).  Known assignment probabilities, conditional randomization, and the three consistency restrictions give, for \(a,z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \frac{p_{x,z,a,1,y_k}}{\pi_z(x)}
 =P\{X=x,D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=a,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1,
 Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=y_k\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Division is valid because instrument positivity gives \(\pi_z(x)\geq\pi_*>0\).  With binary treatments and no defiers,
\[
 \mathbf1\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}-\mathbf1\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\}
 =\mathbf1_{\mathsf C},
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbf1\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=0\}-\mathbf1\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=0\}
 =\mathbf1_{\mathsf C}.
\tag{3}
\]
Substitution of (1)--(3) into the displayed contrast therefore proves the identifying equality
\[
 c_{axk}(p)=P\{X=x,\mathsf C,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1,
 Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=y_k\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the observed law identifies the selected-complier submeasures; this is not a definition of their causal interpretation.

Within stratum \(x\), weak directional selection monotonicity makes the two selected-complier events nested.  If \(s(x)=1\), the smaller event is \(S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\); if \(s(x)=-1\), it is \(S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\).  Hence, with \(\mathsf A=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\),
\[
 m_x=\min\{q_{0x},q_{1x}\}=P(X=x,\mathsf C,\mathsf A),
 \qquad
 M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(\mathsf C,\mathsf A)\geq m_*>0.
\tag{5}
\]
The last inequality is the aggregate-target-positivity restriction and makes every following conditional quantile well defined.

For a compatible law, put
\[
 R_{ax}(j)=P\{X=x,\mathsf C,\mathsf A,
 Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)\leq y_j\}.
\tag{6}
\]
This is a submeasure of the selected-complier measure in (4), has total mass \(m_x\), and is obtained from a measure of total mass \(q_{ax}\) by deleting mass \(q_{ax}-m_x\).  Therefore
\[
 [C_{ax}(j)-q_{ax}+m_x]_+
 \leq R_{ax}(j)\leq\min\{m_x,C_{ax}(j)\},
\tag{7}
\]
which is exactly \(L_{ax}(j)\leq R_{ax}(j)\leq U_{ax}(j)\).  Summing (7) over \(x\), dividing by the positive denominator in (5), and applying the finite-grid generalized inverse gives
\[
 Q_a^-(t)\leq Q_{a,P}(t)\leq Q_a^+(t).
\tag{8}
\]
Thus the capacity formulas are observable-law marginal outer bounds.  They are not being declared equal to the causal quantiles.

Fiber-polytope equivalence shows that optimization over \(\Xi(p)\) neither omits nor adds any member of \(\mathcal F(p)\).  The lower- and upper-endpoint attainment propositions then give, separately for every \(t\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_{1,P_t^-(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p)}(t)&=\underline\Delta(t;p),\\
 Q_{1,P_t^+(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p)}(t)&=\overline\Delta(t;p),
 \end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
with both quantiles in either line generated by the same compatible law.  For any \(P\in\mathcal F(p)\), the definitions of infimum and supremum imply
\[
 \underline\Delta(t;p)\leq\Delta_P(t)\leq\overline\Delta(t;p).
\tag{10}
\]
Taking all coordinates in (10) proves the outer, not necessarily sharp rectangular, inclusion
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p)
 \subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
 [\underline\Delta(t;p),\overline\Delta(t;p)].
\tag{11}
\]

For the tangent conclusion, take the same observed base \(p_0=p(P_0)\).  Under the stated relative-interior and image conditions, the relative-interior tangent-lift lemma proves lawfulness of every direction \(Bu\), and the global-cover proposition gives closed rational cells covering \(\mathbb R^d\).  Because \(p_0\in\Delta^\circ(\mathcal J)\) and \(B\) has rank \(d\),
\[
 x'B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}Bx
 =\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0
 \quad(x\ne0).
\tag{12}
\]
Thus \(I_0\succ0\) and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\).  When \((p_0,B)\) is rational, both matrices are rational.  The radius proposition supplies \(H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing\).  The finite rational cell construction, (3), (12), the rational metric and honesty level, and this nonempty separated domain verify respectively every member condition in \(\mathfrak E\).  Therefore \(\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E\).  The construction used only the affine directional slacks at the compatible base and nowhere treated \(p_0+Bu\) as an observed probability law.

Put \(q=49/25\), \(k=\sqrt{3/10}\), and \(s=\sqrt{13/10}\), and whiten \(w=(a,b)\) to

\tag{1}

Every displayed row of every \(F_v\) has Euclidean norm one.  If \(h\in D_v\), both inward standardized facet means are nonnegative.  Thus the union bound gives

Rational interval evaluation of \((2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_q^\infty e^{-x^2/2}\,dx\), using range-reduced exponential series on rational subintervals and bounding each remainder by the first omitted alternating term, gives

\tag{3}

Therefore \(2\Phi(-49/25)<0.0499957902966<1/20\).  Equations (2)--(3) prove global \(0.95\) coverage, including all equality faces.

Now let \(h\in H_2\) have unique label \(v\).  Since the other three cones form the complement of the interior of \(D_v\), and \(D_v\) is the intersection of its two unit inward halfspaces, distance at least two from every rival implies that both standardized inward facet means are at least two. \tag{4}

\tag{5}

Direct differentiation along the diagonal yields

\tag{6}

The centered integral in polar coordinates is

 \Phi_2(0,0;\rho_*)
 =\frac14-\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}.
\tag{7}
\]
Integrating (6) from \(0\) to \(t\), and using \(0\leq\ell\leq1\), proves

The alternating series for \(\arctan x\) at \(x=\sqrt{3/10}<1\), together with the same outward Gaussian integral calculation used in (3), gives
\[
 0.0797514300099<\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}<0.0797514300101,
\tag{9}

and

The right side of (8) is therefore below \(0.8137979931574<0.813799\).

For the lower certificate, set \(\mu_\pm=(\pm1/\sqrt2,2)\) and \(\mu_0=(0,2)\).  In whitened coordinates, \(\mu_+\) is at standardized distance two from the rival halfspace across \(a=0\), and at distance greater than two from the remaining rival cones; symmetry gives the same conclusion for \(\mu_-\).  Hence \(\mu_\pm\in H_2\).  After integrating the common second coordinate, write the standardized first coordinate as \(z\).  The risk-mixture density divided by \(\phi(z)\) equals

\tag{11}

Under the discrete label metric, pointwise minimization over actions in the displayed dual reduces to the minimum of this risk-mixture density and \(\lambda\phi(z)\): a singleton \(02\) or \(12\) costs \(\lambda\phi(z)\), while an action containing both costs the risk density, and all other actions are weakly more expensive.  Put
\[
 a_0=1028/625,\qquad \lambda_0=e^{-2}\cosh(2a_0).
\tag{12}

The two curves cross at \(z=\pm a_0\), so the dual value at \(\lambda_0\) is

Finally take \(r=0\).  All four regions meet at the origin, so global honesty gives

Write \(\psi_j(p)=\alpha_j'p+\beta_j\).  Affinity and the definition of the moving remainder give the exact identity
\[
 e_{n,j}(u)=\alpha_j'
 \left(\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right).
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\) is finite, Cauchy--Schwarz implies, for every rational compact polytope \(C\),
\[
 \max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|
 \leq\left(\max_j\|\alpha_j\|_2\right)
 \sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right\|_2
 \longrightarrow0
\tag{2}
\]
by the compact-uniform local-expansion assumption.  When the active set is empty, the maximum is zero by convention.

Base convergence and \(\min_j(p_0)_j\geq\kappa>0\) imply that every coordinate of \(p_n(0)\) is eventually at least \(\kappa/2\).  Coordinatewise reciprocal is continuous on that set, and therefore
\[
 B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B
 \longrightarrow B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}B=I_0.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(x\ne0\), full column rank of \(B\) and positivity of \(p_0\) give
\[
 x'I_0x=\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(I_0\) is positive definite.  Matrix inversion is continuous on the positive-definite cone, so (3)--(4) and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\) yield
\[
 [B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B]^{-1}\longrightarrow\Sigma_0.
\tag{5}
\]
